title: Your end-to-end design project
idea: The mid-course project asks you to design one system from this chapter on your own, from requirements to a running demo, using one repeatable checklist.
points: Pick a system you found hard: a booking system, cache, rate limiter or logger.
Write the brief before code; it is your interview answer in written form.
For every pattern you use, name the change it protects you from.
Finish with a demo script that shows the main flow and one failure.

hero.title: Six steps from prompt to demo

items.label: Scope
items.text: Pick one system. List its must-have actions and what is out of scope.

items.label: Entities
items.text: Underline the nouns. Keep those that hold state or enforce a rule.

items.label: Responsibilities
items.text: Give each class one job and a few public methods. Draw the has-a links.

items.label: Change points
items.text: Mark what is likely to change. Put each behind an interface or strategy.

items.label: Core flow
items.text: Code the main use case end to end in a small runnable script.

items.label: Break it
items.text: Try invalid input, no free capacity and two users at once. Fix what fails.

code.title: Design brief template
code.caption: Copy this into your project folder and fill each section before writing classes. Keep it to one page.

pitfalls: Do not start coding before the brief lists both requirements and out-of-scope items.
If one class holds most methods, split its jobs into smaller classes.
Do not add a pattern unless you can name the change it isolates.

quiz.q: You start the project on a hotel booking system. What do you settle first?
options: Which design patterns the solution will use
The must-have actions and what is out of scope
The database tables and their indexes
A class name for every noun in the prompt
quiz.why: Scope decides which entities matter. Patterns, storage and class names follow from the requirements, not the other way round.

takeaway: Scope first, classes second, patterns only where change is expected.

starters: Which system from this chapter is best for practising concurrency?
